Lean Pool now has exposition!

Exposition is a better version of lean docs. It is used by @Rémy Degenne's is his Machine Learning formalization project. My favorite feature is the dependency graph and dependency cone extraction. You can also get the Minimal Lean File for a given theorem to make it easier to audit the statement (this part is WIP because it's hard to reliably extract dependencies across files in arbitrary Lean code).

Lean Pool now has Challenges!

Right now there are two challenges, Mizar's theorem and Odlyzko's bound, both taken directly from FLT/Assumptions. Whoever solves a challenge can PR it to LeanPool, Comparator will check the solution and if it compiles, it will get merged.

There are two ways to interact with Challenges:

  1. You can solve a challenge. Just direct your AI at it or hand-code your solution or do a mix of both - whatever you prefer!
  2. You can propose a challenge. This will be very carefully reviewed and assessed on significance and correctness of formalization.

Challenges are similar to TauCeti's roadmaps, except the challenge has to be a single self-contained result as opposed to a whole roadmap. Challenges are also similar to formal-conjectures, but Lean Pool stays up to date with mathlib, has fast review and fast merges and more citizen-science spirit :)

Let's crowdsource our way to FLT and beyond!
